mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level (as of the decision date) is inversely related to S&P 500 returns: lower rates compress discount rates, leading to positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The rank IC of FEDFUNDS level on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS is below the 25th percentile is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1.5% (as of the decision date), it predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% (as of decision date), or the rank IC of FEDFUNDS threshold on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, when unemployment rate is below 4.5% and GDP growth (annualized) exceeds 2.0%, it predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to strong economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return when UNRATE < 4.5% and GDPC1 growth > 2.0% is negative, or the rank IC of the joint condition on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, housing market strength (HOUST above 1200) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to robust consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST exceeds 1200, or the rank IC of HOUST threshold on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% (as of the decision date), it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days due to recessionary fears and reduced consumer confidence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the rank IC of UNRATE threshold on 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a stagflation regime, when inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% and unemployment (UNRATE) is below 4.0%, it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to policy tightening and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: The average 60-day return when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4.0% is positive, or the rank IC of the joint condition on 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The industrial production index (INDPRO) level is positively correlated with S&P 500 returns: higher industrial output signals strong economic activity, leading to positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The rank IC of INDPRO level on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when INDPRO is above the 75th percentile is not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%), the S&P 500 is expected to have negative returns over the next 60 days due to central bank tightening and reduced real earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or the rank IC of CPIAUCSL threshold on 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
